pages.text: [[Area]] is how many unit squares cover a shape. This floor is 3 rows of 4 one-metre squares, so 4 × 3 = 12 m². Drag its corner to try others.

pages.name: Area, not around
pages.task: A plant room floor is 6 m by 4 m. What is its area?
pages.why: Area counts the squares inside. 4 rows of 6 one-metre squares is 6 × 4 = 24 m².

pages.name: Draw the floor
pages.task: A floor has a 3 m side and covers 12 m². Drag the corner to draw it.
pages.why: With a 3 m side, 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so the other side is 4 m. The floor is 4 m by 3 m, or 3 m by 4 m.

pages.name: Half a rectangle
pages.text: Cut a rectangle corner to corner and the two halves match. So each half is a triangle covering 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 m².

pages.name: A bracket plate
pages.task: A triangular bracket plate has these sides. What is its area?
pages.why: The 40 cm and 30 cm sides meet at a square corner, so they are the base and height. 40 × 30 ÷ 2 = 600 cm². The 50 cm side is not used.

pages.text: Slide the top corner along and the triangle is still half its rectangle. Its [[height]] is the 4 m at right angles to the base, not a sloping side.

pages.name: Which height?
pages.why: The height at right angles to the 6 cm base is 4 cm. 6 × 4 ÷ 2 = 12 cm². The 5 cm sides slope, so they are not used.

pages.text: Split an L-shaped floor into rectangles and add, 12 + 6 = 18 m². Or take the missing corner from the whole, 20 − 2 = 18 m².

Or the whole 20 square metres minus the missing 2 square metre corner, 18 square metres.

pages.name: An L-shaped room
pages.task: What is the floor area of this L-shaped room?
pages.why: The right part is 6 − 4 = 2 m wide and 5 − 3 = 2 m tall, 4 m². With the 4 m by 5 m part, 20 + 4 = 24 m².

pages.name: Around the room
pages.task: A cable runs once around the edge of the same room. How long is that run?
pages.why: The two unlabelled sides are 6 − 4 = 2 m and 5 − 3 = 2 m. Around the edge, 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 6 = 22 m.
